mechanism_narrative: The 9.1-point week-on-week rise in RETAIL_REC from t-1w to t-0w is a persistent recovery impulse; because retail footfall has already broken above its four-week mean, the next 28 days will average higher than the previous 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -32.7 to -23.6 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days despite the t-0w rebound.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS crossing above -5 percent change from baseline marks the summer outdoor-leisure regime in Greater London; this complements rather than substitutes for retail-and-recreation trips, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -5 percent change from baseline.
failure_condition: When PARKS is above -5, mean RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is lower than its trailing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Retail recovery is jointly constrained by commuting and public-transport use: unless TRANSIT rises above -30 and WORKPLACES rises above -20, the t-0w retail bounce will decay as worker and shopper flows remain too weak to sustain it.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -30 and WORKPLACES falls below -20.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -32.0 and WORKPLACES is -21.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -30 and WORKPLACES remains below -20.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-lockdown summer-holiday regime, elevated RESIDENTIAL above 19 and positive GROCERY_PHARM above 4 indicate home-centered households that make local discretionary trips; this keeps RETAIL_REC above its recent 28-day mean over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at t-0w is 20.1 and GROCERY_PHARM is 5.3
failure_condition: With RESIDENTIAL above 19 and GROCERY_PHARM above 4, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is below its trailing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A policy-easing impulse is visible when TRANSIT crosses above -30 percent change from baseline; this reduces the friction cost of retail trips and lifts RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -30 percent change from baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at t-0w is -32.0, within 2 points of -30
failure_condition: Following a TRANSIT crossing above -30, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than its trailing 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A work-from-home configuration in which WORKPLACES stays below -20 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 20 shifts spending toward local high streets; the interaction of these two series predicts higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at t-0w is -21.7 and RESIDENTIAL is 20.1
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES is below -20 and RESIDENTIAL is above 20, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than its trailing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: School summer holidays in Greater London raise leisure-oriented footfall; if PARKS remains above -15 and RETAIL_REC remains above -25 through the holiday period, RETAIL_REC will average higher over the next 28 days than over the past 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at t-0w is -3.7 and RETAIL_REC is -23.6
failure_condition: Under PARKS > -15 and RETAIL_REC > -25, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains positive above +5 while RETAIL_REC stays below -20, essential spending is absorbing household budgets and crowding out discretionary retail, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at t-0w is 5.3 and RETAIL_REC is -23.6
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM > 5 and RETAIL_REC < -20, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its trailing 14-day mean.
